The *Oṭṭhanillehaka-sikkhāpada* (Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Sekhiya 54) is a training rule for Buddhist monastics cataloged in the Vinaya Piṭaka, addressing proper etiquette and deportment during meals—specifically regulating against licking one's lips while eating [SuttaCentral]. An English translation of the rule has been prepared by Bhikkhu Brahmali under the title *Licking the lips* [SuttaCentral].
SuttaCentral notes full canonical parallels across several Vinaya lineages and recensions, including the Bhikkhu Pātimokkha (*pli-tv-bu-pm-sk54*), the Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga (*pli-tv-bi-vb-sk54*), the Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha (*pli-tv-bi-pm-sk54*), both the Bhikkhu and Bhikkhunī Parivāra Sekhiya lists, and a Chinese parallel preserved in the Upāliparipṛcchā (*lzh-upp-bu-sk40*) [SuttaCentral].
